But what I'd like to do, because we have very limited time, Mr. Tolimir, is I'd like to simply ask you if there's any particular health matters that you wish to bring to my attention today, not the matters that you've already dealt with by way of your submissions, because those are all -- will all be considered, but anything particular you want to bring to my attention today. And as I say, our time is quite limited at this stage. Mr. Tolimir, is there anything you wanted to bring to my attention regarding your health today? THE ACCUSED TOLIMIR: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I wanted to reply to the issue you posed at the end of the discussion of my arrest. You said, "Does anybody wish to say anything," and I wish to say just two sentences. The morality is the basis of any innocence, and the morality of all of those people who put forward false facts and inform both this Tribunal and the public must be penalized. I, as a religious person, value morality above anything else in any task, and I believe this is a precondition for anything -- for me to participate in anything. This is why I ask that you resolve the issue of my arrest. Once you resolve that issue, then you can decide on all other issues. Second, it is not proper to tell me that I should not have the right to self-represent myself because I insist on the issue of my arrest be resolved, and because I insist that I be served anything in Cyrillic script. You just told me now that I can not even receive transcript from this session in Cyrillic. What is this but discrimination? Who has discriminated against me? I cannot receive the transcript from this session today in Serbian, in the Cyrillic script. Can you rule on that? If you can, then I will abide by your ruling. But nobody dares to rule on this. Why not? What is the problem there? Why is the Cyrillic script such a problem to this Tribunal, when it can be easily resolved by a computer programme? I ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Tolimir. We're not able to return once again to the issues that we have already covered at great length. I've taken your -- THE ACCUSED TOLIMIR: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I've taken your points in relation to that issue and the arrest issue, and we need to bring the matters to a conclusion. I simply want to deal, finally, with the issue of health, Mr. Tolimir. Is there anything you wish to bring to my attention regarding health or any other issue, not revisiting the issues that we've already covered? THE ACCUSED TOLIMIR: [Interpretation] Thank you. I want to tell you that my health is excellent, and I thank you for asking me that question, so that the people who are interested in my health can hear about it. But I would like to ask you that we discuss three of my motions which regard the violation of my discretionary right, not to discuss my health. We can't equate this, my discretionary rights and my health. So if you would like to discuss the violation of my discretionary rights, that's what I would like to do, and I have expounded upon them in my three submissions ranging between five and six pages. If we can't do that now, then we can do that at another conference and I can write more submissions. But I don't think there's any point to that, because for three months I have been writing submissions about the violation of my discretionary rights, but nobody has reacted and no measures are taken. So I don't see any reason for us -- or purpose in us discussing anything else if the problems I raise are not acted upon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tolimir, I'm well aware of the submissions that you've made, and I certainly do agree with you that those submissions need to be responded to and addressed. As you probably know, though, there is the procedure in place where the initial response and subsequent responses actually to those kinds of submissions have to come through the commanding officer and then through the Registrar, and, ultimately potentially, the President. So they are -- you have made those submissions. The Registry is aware of them, and I will certainly indicate to the Registry that there should be responses to those. But the way the procedure works, Mr. Tolimir, there's not much that I can do today in relation to those motions. But I will make sure to bring to the attention of the Registry your request today that those be responded to, the motions that you have brought regarding conditions at the unit, and we will take the matter up again, if there's been no progress, at the next Status Conference that we hold. So, certainly, I agree with you that those motions are pending and need to be addressed, but the procedure is such that it falls to the responsibility of the Registry at an initial phase. So, for today, we will leave it at that. And unless there is any other particular issue you wanted to bring to my attention, Mr. Tolimir, those were all of the issues that I had intended to raise today, or if the Prosecution has any additional issues. I'll perhaps first hear from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one very brief issue. Since the General is now representing himself, I would just like to pass on, well, to you, Madam President and the General, that we are open to discuss motions or anything else with him, as we would any party. Also, the Prosecutor has invited General Tolimir to speak to her, if he so chooses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Tolimir, any further -- any comments or any further matters that you want to raise today? THE ACCUSED TOLIMIR: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to respond to the question raised by the Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey. I would like to thank him, first and foremost. But as I am defending myself, I don't wish to talk to the Prosecutor, and I refuse to talk to Carla Del Ponte, too, because there was no purpose to that meeting, and I had the right to refuse a meeting. And I can tell you here and now that I don't wish to speak to the Prosecutor about the issues that he wanted to discuss with me, which are not linked to these proceedings and the trial. Secondly, I don't wish to discuss any matters or any plea bargaining or anything like that or any deals, and I don't have anything to discuss with the Prosecution until the question of my arrest has been solved, because I cannot build proper proceedings on the basis of the fact that I was not arrested properly. Now, if I am presumed innocent, how can I believe in what we discuss if, at the beginning, at the starting point, we show a lack of understanding and use certain things that are not -- that do not correspond to the truth? So could you bear that in mind, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: I will certainly bear in mind that, Mr. Tolimir, and the whole of our discussion today, and I re-emphasise the Trial Chamber shares your concern about the serious allegations you have raised with respect to your arrest. The issue has not been dealt with, but will be dealt with in due course. So I will certainly keep in mind all of the matters that you have raised today. If there's nothing further from the Prosecution or from you, Mr. Tolimir, and you apparently have no other matters you wish to bring to my attention, especially regarding your health, I will simply close, once again, with exhorting you again to please consider following the requests of the medical authorities, in terms of your medication. I know that you've discussed this issue at length, but I simply add my voice to the request, for your own health interests, that you do comply with the requests of the medical doctors who are advising you. And with that, there is nothing further for today. We will have another Status Conference in due course. Mr. Tolimir, you will be notified in advance, as you were this time, about a potential Status Conference in the future. Otherwise, we are adjourned for the afternoon. Mr. Tolimir, did you have something you wish to say? THE ACCUSED TOLIMIR: [Interpretation] I do. I would like to ask you to let me know in advance and not two hours before the Status Conference, about when the Status Conference will take place. So please enable me to have enough time to contact my legal adviser, which is something that I have a right to do, just like anybody else defending themselves. And I ask this time, too, that my legal adviser comes to The Hague so that I can talk to him before I appear at the Status Conference. That was not allowed. And I understand you question my right to defend myself, but that was a right accorded to me by the Statute. So please don't -- I don't want to make it that my health is a problem here. My health is not the problem. I am in very good health. The problem is you don't want to deal with other problems related to my arrest, and then you wish to bring to the fore my health and to question my discretionary rights. My health has not influenced my work in any way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: We have your points on those issues. We are adjourned, and I wish everyone a good afternoon and weekend. Thank you.
